editor.fault.replicaNumber.description: The menu lists the first {count} replicas. Enter any other replica number here; leave empty to target the whole group or all outgoing-call copies.
editor.fault.target.description: A block or original connection targets all its copies. Use service#k or connection#k for one replica or outgoing-call copy. Clients, routers and request connections cannot be fault targets.
editor.fault.from.description: The interval is [from, to): the start is included and the end is excluded. Times include warm-up.
editor.fault.to.description: The end must be after the start and no later than warm-up + measurement.
editor.fault.multiplier.description: During the fault: sample × multiplier + delay. Set at least a multiplier or an added delay. Overlapping slowdowns multiply their factors and add their delays.
editor.fault.delay.description: During the fault: sample × multiplier + delay. An absent multiplier is 1; an absent delay is 0. The delay uses explicit duration units.
editor.fault.failureRate.description: On blocks, this replaces the normal local error probability. On connections, transmission fails without work at the destination. Overlapping faults combine as p + q × (1 − p).
editor.fault.capacity.description: Available slots during the fault, from 0 to the target's nominal capacity. Running work completes; new arrivals use the reduced capacity.
editor.fault.kind.slowdown.description: Processing time on blocks or network delay on connections becomes sample × multiplier + delay.
editor.fault.kind.errors.description: Errors replace the local error probability on blocks or reject transmission on connections. Overlapping probabilities combine as p + q × (1 − p).
editor.fault.kind.unavailable.descriptio: An immediate error before work is accepted or the request is transmitted. The caller can retry immediately.
editor.fault.kind.blackhole.description: No response or work at the destination. The caller waits until its timeout or deadline.
editor.fault.kind.capacityLoss.descripti: Reduces available handlers or connections to the specified capacity. Only targets with a slot pool support this kind; routes and calls without a pool do not.

catalog.assumptions.0: Summary metrics use the cohort of original requests arriving during the measurement interval; their outcomes and caused attempts include run-out.
catalog.assumptions.1: Time series use event-time windows covering warmup and measurement; run-out is excluded from series windows.
catalog.assumptions.2: Latency quantiles use the ddsketch-bitwise6-rational-v1 profile with KSL interpolation; representation error is at most 0.78125% in the tested 0.001–60000 ms range.
catalog.assumptions.3: Means over independent replications use Student 95% confidence intervals; interval bounds are not clipped to physical metric ranges.
catalog.types.client.title: Client
catalog.types.client.description: Open Poisson stream of original requests with an end-to-end deadline.
catalog.types.client.assumptions.0: Requests arrive as an open Poisson stream; each original request has an absolute end-to-end deadline.
catalog.types.client.assumptions.1: After the deadline the client stops waiting, but admitted work continues.
catalog.types.client.params.deadline.des: End-to-end deadline of each original request. Initially 10s.
catalog.types.service.title: Service
catalog.types.service.description: Blocking service: a handler is held through local work, downstream calls and backoff.
catalog.types.service.assumptions.0: A handler is allocated once and held through local processing, all downstream attempts, and backoff; retries do not re-enter the caller queue.
catalog.types.service.assumptions.1: An upstream timeout or deadline does not release downstream handlers or remove admitted work.
catalog.types.service.params.queue.title: Queue capacity
catalog.types.service.params.queue.descr: Waiting places in the FIFO queue. 0 means no queue: when all handlers are busy, an attempt is rejected immediately. Initially 100.
Local processing time of one attempt. Initially exponential with a mean of 10ms.
Choose fixed for a constant duration, exponential for independent random durations, or lognormal for a long tail of slow operations.
Use the measured average, not p95 or p99. It sets the scale of the chosen distribution.
For lognormal only: use the measured standard deviation. Larger values produce more variation.
catalog.types.service.params.failureRate: Probability that one local attempt fails.
catalog.types.request.title: Request
catalog.types.request.description: Delivers original requests from the client to the entry service without delay or retries.
catalog.types.request.assumptions.0: Client requests enter the first service without network delay, per-attempt timeout, or retries.
catalog.types.call.title: Call
catalog.types.call.description: Synchronous call with a per-attempt timeout, retries and backoff on the caller side.
catalog.types.call.assumptions.0: A timeout stops the caller from waiting; it does not cancel downstream work, which remains as orphaned work and continues consuming resources.
catalog.types.call.assumptions.1: Late responses are discarded after timeout or deadline.
catalog.types.call.assumptions.2: Cancellation does not propagate along the call chain.
catalog.types.call.params.network.title: Network delay
catalog.types.call.params.network.descri: One-way network delay, drawn separately for the request and the response. Initially fixed at 1ms.
catalog.types.call.params.network.kind.d: Choose fixed for a constant duration, exponential for independent random durations, or lognormal for a long tail of slow operations.
catalog.types.call.params.network.mean.d: Use the measured average, not p95 or p99. It sets the scale of the chosen distribution.
catalog.types.call.params.network.stdDev: For lognormal only: use the measured standard deviation. Larger values produce more variation.
catalog.types.call.params.timeout.title: Timeout
catalog.types.call.params.timeout.descri: Per-attempt timeout, also bounded by the remaining deadline. Initially 1s.
catalog.types.call.params.attempts.title: Attempts
catalog.types.call.params.attempts.descr: Maximum attempts including the first one.
catalog.types.call.params.backoff.title: Backoff
catalog.types.call.params.backoff.kind.d: Fixed uses the base delay, capped by the maximum. Exponential pauses choose a random value from zero to the current limit; the multiplier sets how that limit changes.
catalog.types.call.params.backoff.base.d: Delay after the first failed attempt before jitter.
catalog.types.call.params.backoff.max.de: Upper bound of one backoff delay.

messages.LINT_TIMEOUT_BUDGET: Timeout {timeoutMs} ms is shorter than the estimated {requiredMs} ms for downstream processing and calls. Replies may arrive too late; increase this timeout or reduce downstream timeouts and retries.
messages.LINT_TIMEOUT_UNREACHABLE: Timeout {timeoutMs} ms on connection '{connection}' is at least {threshold} × deadline for these clients (deadlines in ms): {clientDeadlines}. Their deadlines expire first; reduce the timeout so it can protect these requests.
messages.LINT_TIMEOUT_UNREACHABLE_DETAIL: The rule compares the call timeout with each client deadline on paths that use the connection: timeout ≥ threshold × deadline, with threshold 1 by default. Clients appear once across request types and router branches. Inner and outer call timeouts are compared separately by LINT_TIMEOUT_BUDGET.
messages.LINT_RETRY_NO_JITTER: Connection '{connection}' allows {attempts} attempts with backoff '{backoff}', above the warning threshold of {threshold}. Retries may synchronize and overload dependencies; use exponential-full-jitter.
messages.LINT_RETRY_NO_JITTER_DETAILS: The rule warns when attempts > threshold (1 by default) and backoff.kind is none or fixed. Attempts include the first call. A retry budget limits the number of retries but does not stagger them. Only calls on applicable client and request type paths are checked.
messages.LINT_RETRY_AMPLIFICATION: Nested retries allow up to {amplification} attempts per request, above the warning threshold of {threshold}. Failures may overload dependencies; reduce attempts at one or more layers.
messages.LINT_HANDLERS_LITTLE: {elementType}: {handlers}; estimated simultaneous demand: {demand} at {ratePerSecond} requests/s. Queues may grow; increase capacity or reduce load or processing time.
messages.LINT_DEADLINE_BUDGET: Deadline {deadlineMs} ms is shorter than the entry service's estimated {requiredMs} ms. The client may stop waiting before completion; increase its deadline or reduce the entry call's timeout and retries.
messages.LINT_FEW_REPLICATIONS: Only {replications} independent replications: 95% confidence intervals are unreliable. Use at least {minimum} replications before comparing results.
messages.LINT_TIMEOUT_BUDGET_DETAILS: The estimate adds request and response network means, target processing, downstream attempts × timeout, and maximum backoffs. Shortfalls within 5% of this timeout are tolerated; these are configured reserves, not a prediction of actual latency.
messages.LINT_RETRY_AMPLIFICATION_DETAIL: Multiply the maximum attempts at each layer, including the first attempt. This is an upper bound during failures, not the expected number of attempts.
messages.LINT_HANDLERS_LITTLE_DETAILS: λ·W / 1000 = {demand}: λ = {ratePerSecond} requests/s, W = {holdingMs} ms of handler occupancy. The peak client rate is split by routing; least-in-flight assumes equal conditions. This conservative estimate excludes queues, failures, retries and timeout truncation.
messages.LINT_DEADLINE_BUDGET_DETAILS: The entry budget adds local processing, outgoing attempts × timeout, and maximum backoffs. Nested timeouts and network delays already inside that timeout are not added again.
messages.LINT_FEW_REPLICATIONS_DETAILS: The rule compares independent replications with the minimum of {minimum}; it does not compare requests or time windows. Warnings do not block a run.
messages.LINT_SCENARIO_UNUSED_DETAILS: The rule compares outgoing connections with call steps in the effective service scenario.
messages.LINT_BALANCING_IGNORED_DETAILS: A call's balancing setting selects target replicas only when the target is a replica group. An explicit router uses its own policy.

catalog.types.pooler.title: Transaction pooler
catalog.types.pooler.description: Client admission and a bounded-wait server connection pool before one synchronous call.
catalog.types.pooler.assumptions.0: Transaction mode: client connections have no queue; server connections use a FIFO wait timeout.
catalog.types.pooler.assumptions.1: The server connection is held through local delay and the outgoing call; the client connection lasts through the reply.
catalog.types.pooler.assumptions.2: An upstream timeout does not cancel admitted pooler work.
catalog.types.pooler.params.maxClientCon: Concurrent client connections; excess attempts are rejected immediately. Initially 1000.
catalog.types.pooler.params.poolSize.des: Concurrent server connections held through local delay and the outgoing call. Initially 20.

catalog.types.pooler.params.processing.d: Local delay after acquiring a server connection, before the outgoing call. Initially fixed at 0.1ms.
catalog.types.pooler.params.processing.k: Choose fixed for a constant duration, exponential for independent random durations, or lognormal for a long tail of slow operations.
catalog.types.pooler.params.processing.m: Use the measured average, not p95 or p99. It sets the scale of the chosen distribution.
catalog.types.pooler.params.processing.s: For lognormal only: use the measured standard deviation. Larger values produce more variation.

help.estimate.artifactSize: Estimated compressed result size on disk. Use it to assess storage requirements before running.
help.estimate.events: Approximate number of simulation events across all tasks. It indicates the amount of computation, including work caused by retries.
help.estimate.parts: Estimated number of result parts stored and loaded separately. More parts mean more files and requests when reading results.
help.estimate.rows: Approximate number of time-window result rows across all tasks. More elements, replications and smaller windows produce more rows to store and read.
help.estimate.time: Approximate elapsed execution time with the indicated workers, based on calibrated measurements. Actual time depends on the model and computer; this is not simulated time or a deadline.
help.estimate.uncompressedSize: Estimated result size before compression. It helps assess the memory and decoded-data budget; the browser loads results in parts.
help.estimate.workers: Number of simulation workers used to estimate elapsed time. Workers execute tasks in parallel; speedup is limited by the calibrated measurements.
help.noAssumptions: No additional assumptions for this type.
help.noOutputs: This type has no output metrics.
help.tasks: One task is one simulation run: variant × grid point × replication. Without a parameter grid, each variant has one point. More tasks increase the total work.

catalog.types.service.params.healthCheck: Probes share the handler queue and processing capacity. All routers skip an instance while it is not ready.
Minimum time between probe starts; the first probe starts after this interval.
Maximum wait for a probe result, including queueing. Admitted processing continues after timeout.
Consecutive failed probes required to mark the initially ready instance not ready.
Consecutive successful probes required to restore readiness.
Local handler time, affected by processing delay faults, without running the request scenario or network.
